newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire government agrees major copper deal.
newsitem.headline: Zaire government agrees major copper deal.

text.p: Zaire's government has agreed to a major copper and cobalt mining deal with a Canadian company -- the first significant investment in the African country by a private mining firm since the 1970s.
The project at Tenke Fungurume in the southern mineral-rich province of Shaba was confirmed by representatives of the company, Consolidated Eurocan Ventures Ltd, and Zairean officials.
It is the first major joint venture between state-run Gecamines and a foreign partner.
Representatives for both sides said that the Zairean cabinet approved the deal at its weekly meeting on Friday.
Government spokesman Boguo Makeli said the cabinet reached a "conclusive decision". Asked if that meant the government had agreed the offer, he replied: "It goes in that direction."

The Kinshasa representative of the Lundin group and Geneva-based Swedish financier Adolf Lundin, who were negotiating on behalf of Eurocan, told Reuters the deal would be signed with state-run mining company Gecamines on Saturday.
Lundin group's Saidi Mbongo said he had seen a copy of the contract letter signed by the deputy prime minister in charge of mines after Friday's cabinet meeting.

Under the deal, Gecamines will have a 45 percent stake in the project and Eurocan a 55 percent stake, sources close to the deal said. Lundin group had a 55 percent stake in Eurocan, a mining and exploration company, they added.
A consortium led by a second Canadian company, Cornucopia Resources, which included metals giants Inco Ltd and Phelps Dodge, had said it was still in the running.
Gecamines and other sources close to the deal said it covered development of deposits which could yield 100,000 tonnes a year of copper and 8,000 tonnes of cobalt.

Sources close to the deal say investment in phase one would be around $350 million. A feasibility study between one and two years could lead to the first production of copper after as little as four and a half years.

Eurocan spokeswoman Sophia Shane said last week Tenke Fungurume, near Zambia, held at least 222 million tonnes of resource grading 4.42 percent copper and 0.33 percent cobalt, according to estimates done before Eurocan's interest.
"We anticipate it will be several times that," she added.
Tenke Fungurume was previously explored by a consortium led by Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd, which invested almost US$300 million in the project but walked away because of political risk.
